value.produces: assets/lisa (LisaEm 2.0 + GTK closure + Rev H ROM + config template) and disk/lisa-profile.dc42.golden (LOS 3.1 ProFile image; cold-boot reset)

labctl.notes: HOST-NATIVE, SANDBOXED: LisaEm 2.0.0 (assets/lisa/lisaem, the upstream AppImage extracted; its GTK 3 closure in assets/lisa/lib) runs — inside a systemd-nspawn container with private PID/mount/net/user namespaces (host uid range 200000+, read-only rootfs skeleton with the host /usr bound in, only the station's work/ and x11/ dirs writable, capabilities dropped, @mount filtered; the operator's host-application rule after the medley incident) — an Apple Lisa 2 (68000 5 MHz, 1 MB, boot ROM rev H, 5 MB ProFile) on the host inside a pinned 720x498 Xvfb on :93; the daemon captures the X root (SH_CAPTURE=x11). No QEMU/QMP, no exec channel, no network. POINTER: ABSOLUTE via XTEST (SH_INPUT_BACKEND=x11test, SH_X11TEST_ABS=1): the root is the Lisa video, LisaEm maps the host pointer 1:1 onto the Lisa mouse; buttons held 150 ms (SH_BTN_MIN_HOLD_MS). Keys: XTEST. The launcher (stations/lisa/x11-runtime.sh) collapses the wx menubar via gtk.css, resizes the window to 720 wide and moves it to y=-42 so only the Lisa is captured — a negative X offset breaks GDK button delivery, so never move it horizontally. Reset=relaunch: fresh copy of disk/lisa-profile.dc42.golden + cold boot; the launcher clicks the ProFile icon at the ROM's STARTUP FROM menu 4 s after launch; desktop ~150 s later. Drive it with xdotool on DISPLAY=:93 from labrun (mousemove X Y mousedown 1 sleep 0.15 mouseup 1) or `labctl shot lisa`. LisaEm's own menus are the collapsed 2 px strip above the root — reach them only by keyboard if ever needed.

render.stationsManifestPrelude: # lisa (VMID 193) — host-native LisaEm 2.0 (Apple Lisa 2, 68000 5 MHz, 1 MB, ROM rev H, ProFile) -> Lisa Office System 3.1, the document-centric 1984 desktop, inside a pinned 720x498 Xvfb whose root is the aspect-corrected Lisa screen. Absolute pointer over XTEST (LisaEm follows the host X pointer 1:1); reset = cold boot from a fresh ProFile copy (~150 s).

pointer.device: host X pointer over XTEST (root coordinates are Lisa pixels; LisaEm maps the pointer 1:1 onto the Lisa mouse) + Lisa keyboard over XTEST keys

museum.arch: Motorola 68000 @ 5 MHz, 1 MB RAM, 720x364 bitmapped display, 5 MB ProFile
eraSoftware: LisaWrite, LisaDraw, LisaCalc, LisaGraph, LisaList, LisaProject and LisaTerminal — the seven Lisa tools
the Lisa Desktop Manager and its document-centric filing (stationery pads, tear-off documents, the Wastebasket)
Preferences, the Clipboard and the Calculator desk accessories
museum.periodBrowser: none — 1984, a decade before the web; the Lisa's network was a serial port and AppleNet that never shipped
museum.blurb: Apple's Lisa (1983) put the mouse, overlapping windows, pull-down menus and drag-and-drop filing in front of the public a year before the Macintosh, at $9,995. Lisa Office System 3.1 (1984) is its last release: a document-centric desktop where you tear a sheet off a stationery pad instead of launching a program, and the machine remembers every open window across a power cycle. The Lisa 2 shown here is the 1984 revision with a Sony 3.5-inch drive and the 5 MB ProFile hard disk.
museum.notes: Live streamhost tile, HOST-NATIVE from birth: LisaEm 2.0.0 (Ray Arachelian, GPL-2.0) runs on the host as a wxGTK application inside a pinned 720x498 Xvfb; the daemon captures the X root and drives XTEST. The Lisa video (LisaEm's aspect-corrected 720x498 for the 720x364 frame buffer with its 1.5:1 pixels) is the whole root: the launcher collapses the GTK menubar with a gtk.css and moves the window to y=-42 so nothing but the Lisa is captured. Boot ROM rev H assembled from the MAME lisa2 romset halves; LOS 3.1 with the seven tools on a pre-installed ProFile image from archive.org (docs/lab/LISA-WAVE.md). Reset = relaunch: a fresh copy of the golden ProFile image and a cold boot; the ROM's STARTUP FROM menu is answered by a click on the ProFile icon from the launcher. No network of any kind: a 1984 Lisa has no TCP/IP. See docs/guests/lisa.md.

emulator.version: 2.0.0 (2026.01.25), upstream Linux AppImage, GTK 3 closure bundled from CT950 (Ubuntu 24.04)
emulator.driver: Lisa 2 (ROM rev H, ProFile on the motherboard parallel port)

network.note: No network device of any kind: LisaEm emulates the Lisa's serial ports and parallel port only, and a 1984 Lisa has no TCP/IP stack. The retronet reservation 10.99.0.41 (tap lisarn0, UIN 19300) is held as the plane's uniqueness ledger only — nothing is attached to it.

reset.mouse: PASS (2026-09-09) — ABSOLUTE over XTEST: SH_X11TEST_ABS=1 moves the host X pointer to root coordinates that ARE Lisa pixels (Xvfb 720x498 == the Lisa video); LisaEm feeds the host pointer position to the Lisa mouse 1:1, so the Lisa's own arrow lands on the commanded pixel. Buttons are XTEST with SH_BTN_MIN_HOLD_MS=150 (an instant press/release is sampled away by LisaEm). Framebuffer-proven on the rig: the ROM's STARTUP FROM icon, the Preferences icon and its check boxes all answered clicks at their pixel targets.
reset.keyboard: OPEN (2026-09-09) — XTEST keys reach LisaEm (the daemon resolved 103 scancodes on the sandboxed display; pacing 40/40) but no typed line has been proven in a LisaWrite document yet: the proof needs Disk → Lisa Write → tear a sheet off the pad → open it → type, each step 20-60 s at 5 MHz. Pointer, single click and double-click (Preferences and the Disk window opened) ARE framebuffer-proven.
reset.fixture: Lisa Office System 3.1 desktop at rest: the grey stipple desktop with the Desk / File/Print / Edit / Housekeeping menu bar, Preferences, Wastebasket and Clipboard icons along the bottom and the ProFile 'Disk' icon at the bottom right, exactly as the pre-installed LOS 3.1 image boots. resetMode=relaunch with no state: the launcher copies disk/lisa-profile.dc42.golden to work/profile.dc42, cold-boots LisaEm (-p), clicks the ProFile icon at the ROM's STARTUP FROM menu, and LOS 3.1 shows its 'Wait' splash for ~150 s before the desktop. Golden = the pristine archive.org image (sha256 bbc97e82d544050c156057fd80e28a7f66a8e24429e7ed28442fe9d62b84e2ae); nothing is baked from a running session.
